items.title: Year-end close for 2026

items.title: Partners: 2026 Q4 estimated tax
items.who: Each partner on his own return (Claudio, Ben, Meshach)
items.what: Fourth 2026 estimated payment. The LLC pays no income tax itself; profit or loss passes to each partner.
items.why: The LLC shows a loss so far in 2026, so this depends on each partner's other income and withholding. Skip-able if you file the 2026 return by Feb 1, 2027 and pay in full.
docs: Year-to-date share of LLC profit or loss

items.title: 1099-NEC / 1099-MISC for 2026
items.what: File a 1099-NEC for any non-employee paid $2,000+ in 2026 for services (new threshold for 2026 payments). Due Jan 31; that is a Sunday, so Feb 1, 2027.
items.why: Likely none for 2026: no contractor in the ledger reached $2,000. Meshach is a partner, so his pay goes on his K-1, not a 1099 or W-2. Payments by credit card are reported by the card company, not by us.
docs: W-9 from any contractor or attorney we pay

items.title: Get Totni's 2026 1099 for our loads
items.who: Totni sends it; Claudio checks it
items.what: Totni should report the 2026 load pay to Sand Lily Pad LLC under the LLC EIN (ends 0564).
items.why: Several settlements were paid to Meshach. If Totni has Meshach's W-9 instead of the LLC's, the 1099 lands on his SSN and must be fixed (or nominee-reported).
docs: W-9 we gave Totni (name and EIN on it)

items.title: IFTA Q4 2026 fuel tax return
items.who: Totni (carrier) unless the lease names us - check with Totni
items.what: Quarterly fuel tax by state miles. Due the last day of the month after the quarter (Jan 31 is a Sunday).
items.why: Our combination is over 26,000 lb (14,000 + 25,900 = 39,900), so it is an IFTA qualified vehicle. On a 30+ day lease the carrier reports unless the written lease makes the owner-operator the licensee. Our Totni lease is silent on IFTA, so Totni should be filing.
docs: Fuel receipts with gallons and state

items.title: Partnership return + K-1s (2026)
items.who: Sand Lily Pad LLC (CPA prepares; Claudio signs as tax contact)
items.what: First return: short year Sep 3 to Dec 31, 2026. K-1 to Claudio, Ben and Meshach by the same date. Form 7004 extends to Sep 15, 2027 (no extension for tax the partners owe).
items.why: Multi-member LLC taxed as a partnership (company agreement: Form 1065 and K-1s). No S-corp election (Form 2553) on file. Late penalty: $260 per partner per month (2026 returns), up to 12 months.

items.title: Partners' 2026 personal returns
items.what: Each partner reports his K-1 share on Schedule E, and self-employment tax on Schedule SE where it applies.
items.why: Pass-through: the LLC itself owes no federal income tax.

items.title: Partners: 2027 Q1 estimated tax
items.what: First 2027 estimated payment (Apr 15, Jun 15, Sep 15, then Jan 18, 2028). Confirm on the 2027 Form 1040-ES when the IRS posts it.
items.why: Owed once the LLC is profitable. The draft company agreement sets aside 30% of each owner's profit share for tax.

items.title: Florida annual report (only if registered)
items.who: LLC, only if it registers in Florida as a foreign LLC
items.what: Foreign LLCs registered in Florida file between Jan 1 and May 1; $138.75, plus $400 if late.
items.why: We are a Texas LLC. No Florida registration is on file. The truck is based in Jacksonville; ask the CPA or attorney whether that is transacting business in Florida (interstate commerce alone is not). Florida has no personal income tax, and its corporate income tax does not reach a partnership with individual partners.

items.title: Texas franchise: Public Information Report
items.what: First Texas report. Due May 15; 2027 falls on a Saturday, so Monday May 17. File the PIR on Webfile.
items.why: Revenue is far under the $2.65M no-tax-due threshold, so no franchise tax and no No Tax Due Report, but the PIR is still required or the LLC can lose its right to do business. $50 late-report penalty.

items.title: Partners: 2027 Q2 estimated tax
items.why: Only if a partner expects to owe $1,000+ for 2027.

items.title: Partners: 2027 Q3 estimated tax
items.what: Third 2027 estimated payment. Also the extended 1065 deadline if Form 7004 was filed.
items.why: Only if a partner expects to owe $1,000+ for 2027.

deduction_notes.eld: ELD fees charged by Totni: deductible.
deduction_notes.fuel: Fuel: deductible. Keep gallons and state for IFTA.
deduction_notes.repairs: Repairs and maintenance: deductible. Big upgrades may need to be capitalized.
deduction_notes.insurance: Insurance: deductible. A 12-month prepaid policy can usually be deducted when paid (12-month rule).
deduction_notes.meals: Business meals: 50%. Meals on the road for a driver under DOT hours-of-service rules: 80%.
deduction_notes.overhead: Other overhead: deductible, except the items flagged below.
deduction_notes.notes: Truck and trailer note payments are NOT deductible. Only the interest part is; principal is not. Interest split: not on file.
deduction_notes.legal: Formation/legal: organizational costs, up to $5,000 deductible in year 1, rest over 180 months (Sec. 709).
deduction_notes.title: Trailer title and sales tax: the sales tax adds to the trailer basis (depreciated), registration fees are deductible.
deduction_notes.equipment: Equipment: items over $2,500 each are capitalized unless the CPA says otherwise.
deduction_notes.perdiem: Per diem: transportation M&IE $80/day CONUS from Oct 1, 2026, 80% deductible for HOS drivers. Days away: not on file.
deduction_notes.dep: Depreciation: truck and trailer acquired after Jan 19, 2025 qualify for 100% bonus. Section 179 limit $2.56M (2026) but capped at business income. The Ram is over 6,000 lb GVWR, so no luxury-auto cap; the $32,000 SUV cap does not apply to a pickup with a 6 ft+ bed.

disclaimer: Estimates from our books, not tax advice. Confirm every date and number with the CPA.
